# WHO YOU ARE

Three guides to SETTLE, KANERVA and settle-mcp, one per reader. Each guide says what the three things are in that
reader's own words, how to use them in a project (SETTLE alone, KANERVA alone, and the two together), gives an
example with its output, a basic getting-started, and links into the detailed GUIDE, REFERENCE, EXAMPLES and
COOKBOOK docs of each package.

| folder | reader | opens with |
|---|---|---|
| `for-programmers/` | a computer scientist or programmer, with sections for machine learning and for other problems | a probability model as a program |
| `for-visual-artists/` | someone who makes pictures, films, installations | a picture as fifteen thousand coins |
| `for-sound-artists/` | someone who makes sound, music, instruments | a sound that follows the physics |

The site renders the three on one page, `#/who-you-are`, in that order, with the same Markdown renderer the package
pages use (`src/docs/render.js`). settle-mcp carries the same three files as resources
(`site://who-you-are/for-programmers`, `site://who-you-are/for-visual-artists`, `site://who-you-are/for-sound-artists`)
and its `AGENTS.md` points an assistant at them first; `SETTLE/settle-mcp/tools/build_mcp_docs.mjs`
reads this folder, so an edit here reaches the server on its next build. These files are written in English; the
site's document translator (`tools/i18n_docs.mjs`) lists them as the `whoyouare` set.
